findings.title: Modifying value while iterating with matcher leads to incorrect anchor validation
findings.body: In sanitizeAnchors, `value.replaceFirst(...)` is called inside a loop driven by `matcher.find()` where `matcher` was created from the original `value` string. The `Matcher` holds a reference to the original `CharSequence`, so the loop continues scanning the unmodified string while the replacement mutates `value`. This can cause anchors to be found multiple times, replacements to miss their intended target, or incorrect error reports. The anchor matching logic must be redesigned to avoid mutating the string during iteration (e.g., collect matches first and process them in reverse order).

findings.title: PropertyResourceBundle reads using ISO-8859-1, not UTF-8
findings.body: The `PropertyResourceBundle` is constructed with a `FileInputStream`, which reads properties using ISO-8859-1 encoding by default. Most Keycloak message property files are encoded in UTF-8 (as evidenced by the use of `Files.readString` elsewhere, which defaults to UTF-8). Non-ASCII characters (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic) will be misinterpreted, leading to incorrect sanitization comparisons and false positives/negatives. Use `new InputStreamReader(new FileInputStream(file), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)` when creating the bundle.

findings.title: RuntimeException escapes instead of MojoExecutionException
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() catches `IOException` and throws an unchecked `RuntimeException`. The public `verify()` method declares `MojoExecutionException`, but a RuntimeException can propagate and crash the Maven build with a less descriptive error. This breaks the expected exception contract and makes error handling harder. Wrap the RuntimeException in a MojoExecutionException (or change verifySafeHtml to throw MojoExecutionException).

findings.title: containsHtml pattern is case-sensitive and may miss uppercase tags
findings.body: The regex `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` only matches lowercase tag names. HTML tags are case-insensitive, and the OWASP sanitizer normalizes or handles them case-insensitively. If a translation contains `<B>` while the English source contains `<b>`, containsHtml(englishValue) would be true (if English has lowercase), but the comparison against the translation's uppercase tag would still fail because the sanitized output from OWASP likely normalizes to lowercase, producing a mismatch. The pattern should be case-insensitive (`Pattern.compile("<[a-zA-Z]+[^>]*>"` or with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE`).
